evals.name: straightforward-slice
evals.prompt: Plan this accepted slice for me. Materials are in evals/slice-plan/cases/case-001/: recommendation.md and repo/.
evals.expected_output: A clean, small plan: Goal restates the max-length check; behavioral contract names the 24-char boundary and the exact error message; seams name app/validators.py::validate_username; invariants preserve MIN_LENGTH and the other three checks; verification strategy is the one new boundary test plus the existing suite passing; non-goals match the recommendation's.
expectations: Likely implementation seams names app/validators.py::validate_username specifically (not a new file, not the signup HTTP handler)

Behavioral contract or invariants state the exact boundary (usernames longer than 24 characters rejected, 24 itself still valid) and that MIN_LENGTH and the existing start-with-letter / character-set checks are unaffected

The plan does not introduce anything beyond the accepted slice (e.g. no new configurable max-length setting, no changes to the signup HTTP handler) -- Explicit non-goals matches or is consistent with the recommendation's stated non-goals

expectations: Likely implementation seams names app/serializers.py::serialize_user as the touched seam

Invariants explicitly states that the existing keys serialize_user() already returns (id, email, display_name, created_at) must remain present and unrenamed, grounded in the file's own docstring about downstream consumers depending on the exact key set -- not just asserted without grounding
Invariants or behavioral contract also notes that password_hash must continue to never appear in the serialized payload, even though this slice touches the same function

evals.name: ambiguous-seam-choice

evals.expected_output: The plan implements the SMS call at app/signup_flow.py::handle_signup (the seam the goal's wording -- "when a new user signs up" -- actually points to), not at admin_tools/bulk_import.py, even though bulk_import.py calls the same dispatcher and its rows already carry an optional phone field. Explicit non-goals or Known risks explicitly names that bulk_import.py has its own parallel call to send_welcome_email and was not addressed by this slice, rather than leaving that fact unmentioned

evals.name: underspecified-goal
evals.prompt: Plan this accepted slice for me. Materials are in evals/slice-plan/cases/case-004/: recommendation.md and repo/.
evals.expected_output: The plan adds retry-on-TransientProviderError to attempt_charge(), but explicitly flags that the recommendation never specifies a retry count or backoff schedule -- the chosen number is presented as the smallest reasonable judgment call, not as a spec requirement. The plan doesn't invent unrequested infrastructure (config knobs, metrics, circuit breakers) beyond the retry itself, and preserves that ChargeDeclinedError still raises immediately.
expectations: Known risks (or an equivalent section) explicitly states that the accepted slice does not specify a retry count or backoff schedule, and frames whatever number the plan picks as a judgment call rather than presenting an invented number as if it were a specified requirement

The plan does not add unrequested scope beyond retrying on TransientProviderError -- no new configuration system, no metrics/observability layer, no circuit breaker, no change to how ChargeDeclinedError is raised
Invariants or behavioral contract explicitly preserves that ChargeDeclinedError still raises immediately without any retry, consistent with the recommendation's stated non-goal

evals.name: verification-scoped-to-contract
evals.prompt: Plan this accepted slice for me. Materials are in evals/slice-plan/cases/case-006/: recommendation.md and repo/.
evals.expected_output: Verification strategy adds only tests for the new "-word" exclusion behavior (e.g. basic negation, negation combined with existing must terms) -- it does not propose expanding coverage for the already-tested must/or/fields/quoted-phrase behaviors, and does not propose testing exclusion combined with quoted phrases or field filters (both explicit non-goals). Note: the fixture contains a genuine tension -- the recommendation says existing tests "still pass unchanged," but two existing tests use whole-dict equality that breaks under any added key -- a good plan names this explicitly rather than silently picking a side; either resolution (keep the two tests untouched via a conditional key, or mechanically update their literals) is acceptable.
expectations: Verification strategy specifies new test(s) scoped to the '-word' exclusion behavior only (e.g. basic negation, negation combined with an existing must term), tied to the recommendation's stated acceptance evidence
Verification strategy or explicit non-goals does not propose testing exclusion for quoted phrases or field filters -- both are explicitly out of scope in the recommendation

The plan explicitly names, as a known risk or equivalent, the tension between the recommendation's 'existing tests pass unchanged' claim and the two existing tests (test_single_term, test_empty_query) that use whole-dict equality and would break under any unconditionally-added key -- rather than silently resolving it either way. Either concrete resolution (a conditional must_not key that leaves both tests untouched, or an unconditional key with the two tests' literals mechanically updated) passes, provided the tradeoff is surfaced
